text: World: Epidemic and emerging disease alerts in the Pacific as of 03 November 2026 #Refugees
link_title: World: Epidemic and emerging disease alerts in the Pacific as of 03 November 2026
link_description: Countries: World, Australia, Fiji, Guam, Marshall Islands, Micronesia (Federated States of), New Caledonia (France), New Zealand, Niue (New Zealand), Palau, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Tonga, Tuvalu, Vanuatu, Wallis and Futuna (France) Source: Pacific Community Please refer to the attached Map. Highlights/updates since the last map was sent on PacNet on 27 October 2026: Dengue • American Samoa: The Department of Health Situational Report for 19 to 25 October 2026 records 1,064 laboratory-confirmed dengue cases as of 27 October 2026 since the outbreak began in 2025. New case numbers remain low, with four cases reported over the last three EpiWeeks: two cases in EpiWeek 40 and one case each in EpiWeeks 41 and 42. Dengue cases peaked in early 2026 (EpiWeek 02), with weekly case counts remaining low since May. The blue alert for dengue (DENV-1 & DENV-2) remains in effect. – Source: American Samoa Department of Health, Situational Report: Respiratory & Notifiable Diseases shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 30 October 2026. • Marshall Islands: The 16th Outbreak Situation Report covering 15 August to 22 October 2026, records 165 positive cases (confirmed and probable) among 540 specimens tested: 127 in Majuro and 38 in Ebeye, compared with 124 and 32 cases, respectively, in the previous report covering 15 August to 15 October 2026. There have been 15 hospitalisations (13 in Majuro and two in Ebeye) and no deaths since the beginning of the outbreak. Attack rates are 5.5 per 1,000 population in Majuro and 3.9 per 1,000 in Ebeye, while positivity rates are 29% and 37%, respectively. Only DENV-1 has been identified. Vector control has been completed at the households of 147 positive cases and at 206 sites. About 250 spatial repellents and mosquito nets have been delivered to Ebeye, and surveillance in the neighbouring islands is being strengthened. The red alert for dengue (DENV-1) remains in effect. – Source: Republic of the Marshall Islands Ministry of Health and Human Services, 16th Outbreak Situation Report on dengue fever in Majuro and Ebeye accessed on 03 November 2026. • Samoa: Dengue Fever Outbreak Situation Report Issue No. 79, covering EpiWeek 42 (12 to 18 October 2026), reports 51 new cases, down 4% on the previous week (53, revised from 14), with no laboratory-confirmed case, no new admission and no death. Since 01 January 2025, 20,478 clinically diagnosed cases, 5,547 laboratory-confirmed cases and nine dengue-related deaths have been recorded. DENV-1 accounts for 52% and DENV-2 for 48% of serotyped cases, and children under 15 years for 73% of cases. The blue alert for dengue (DENV-1 & DENV-2) remains in effect. – Source: Ministry of Health Samoa, Dengue Fever Outbreak Situation Report Issue No. 79 accessed on 03 November 2026. Diarrhea • Federated States of Micronesia – Yap State: The Yap weekly bulletin for EpiWeek 43 (19 to 25 October 2026) shows diarrhoea on alert for a tenth consecutive week, rising from 9 to 15 cases, above the alert threshold of 7. All 5 stool specimens tested on the BioFire gastrointestinal panel were positive: three patients had adenovirus, two of them co-infected with E. coli pathotypes, and two had E. coli pathotype co-infections only. Among 100 diarrhoea cases in children aged 0 to 5 years since the start of the outbreak, 34 had completed rotavirus vaccination, 27 were partially vaccinated, 28 were unvaccinated and 11 had their status still being verified. The blue alert for rotavirus is changed to blue alert for diarrhea for the Federated States of Micronesia (Yap State). – Source: Yap State Department of Health Services, Communicable Disease Weekly Bulletin, shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 29 October 2026. Measles • Australia: On 30 October 2026, the Western Australia Department of Health confirmed a new measles case in a young child treated at a Perth hospital. The case is not linked to overseas travel and has no known link to the case reported on 28 October, and the Department says that a locally acquired case with no known source raises concern for undetected community transmission. The earlier case is a returned overseas traveller who visited several public venues in Perth while infectious. People who attended the listed exposure locations are advised to monitor for symptoms and to call ahead before visiting a GP clinic or emergency department. As of 03 November 2026 at the national level, 122 measles notifications have been recorded in Australia, compared with 181 in 2025. The red alert for measles remains in effect for Australia. – Sources: Western Australia Department of Health, Measles alert for Perth in returned overseas traveller , Western Australia Department of Health, WA Health confirms new measles case in young child and Dashboard · NINDSS Portal accessed on 03 November 2026. • Papua New Guinea: The National Department of Health weekly bulletin for EpiWeek 43 (19 to 25 October 2026) reports 26 acute fever and rash cases nationally, down from 30 in EpiWeek 42. Year to date, 452 cases have been reported and 396 samples tested, with 19 IgM-positive measles results. After Expert Review Group review, two measles cases (New Ireland 1, Western Highlands 1) and two rubella cases are confirmed in 2026. The last IgM-positive measles onset was on 15 September 2026 and the last rubella onset on 29 September 2026. The measles-rubella vaccination campaign targets all children under seven in districts with a detected case. The red alert for measles remains in effect for Papua New Guinea. – Source: Papua New Guinea National Department of Health, Public Health Events Weekly Bulletin, shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 30 October 2026. Respiratory diseases • French Polynesia: In French Polynesia, influenza activity increased markedly in EpiWeek 43 (19–25 October 2026), confirming the territory’s entry into an epidemic phase. A total of 52 laboratory-confirmed influenza A cases, predominantly A(H1N1), were reported during the week, with 14 hospitalisations. Increased cases and hospitalisations were observed in Tahiti, Raiatea and the Marquesas, indicating circulation across several parts of the territory. The seasonal influenza vaccination campaign began on 26 October, with vaccination available through pharmacies and health facilities. A red alert for influenza A is issued for French Polynesia. – Source: Agence de régulation de l'action sanitaire et sociale (ARASS), Bulletin de Surveillance Sanitaire de Polynésie française n°38 shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 03 November 2026. • New Zealand: For the week ending 25 October 2026, the all-cause SARI hospitalisation rate in the Auckland region remained stable and in the low activity band. The influenza-positive SARI hospitalisation rate increased slightly but also remained low. Influenza remained the most commonly detected virus among SARI patients, with 17 positive samples, and SARI influenza test positivity increased from 19.0% to 28.3%. Positivity among sentinel GP influenza-like illness cases also increased, from 9.5% to 13.0%. In 2026 to date, 707 of 2,924 (24.2%) SARI samples and 229 of 1,220 (18.8%) sentinel GP samples have tested positive for influenza. The blue alert for influenza A remains in effect for New Zealand. – Source: New Zealand acute respiratory illness dashboard accessed on 03 November 2026. • Tonga: The weekly syndromic surveillance report for EpiWeek 43 (19 to 25 October 2026) shows influenza-like illness (ILI) falling for a second week, from 125 to 84 cases, after the EpiWeek 41 peak of 137. Severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) fell from 13 to 9 cases. From 03 August to 25 October 2026, 89 SARI patients were hospitalised. Of 732 ILI cases, 499 (68.1%) were tested: 235 (47%) were positive for influenza A, 6 for influenza B and 29 for RSV. Four deaths have occurred among SARI cases, unchanged since EpiWeek 42, three of them laboratory-confirmed influenza A. The red alert for influenza A remains in effect for Tonga. – Source: Tonga Ministry of Health, Weekly Communicable Diseases Syndromic Surveillance shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 30 October 2026. Rotavirus • Vanuatu: Situation Update No. 1 on watery diarrhoea on Ambae Island, Penama Province covering 12 to 18 October 2026, reports seven cases in the period, below the weekly alert threshold of 8. Two laboratory-confirmed rotavirus cases were detected in EpiWeek 43, both from Navonda village in East Ambae, confirming ongoing transmission. The Ministry of Health states that the current data do not support an outbreak declaration: from week 1 to week 42, weekly counts at Lolowai Hospital exceeded the threshold only once, in week 10. Most cases are aged over 5 years (59%) and 75% come from East Ambae. One case was admitted and discharged, with no severe case and no death. Enhanced surveillance, active case finding, risk communication on hygiene and safe water, and testing of suspected cases are under way. The red alert for rotavirus is changed to blue alert for rotavirus for Vanuatu. – Source: Vanuatu Ministry of Health, Watery Diarrhoea on Ambae Island, Penama Province, Situation Update No. 1, shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 28 October 2026. Other Information: One Health - High pathogenicity avian influenza • Australia: A dead common dolphin that washed ashore at Encounter Bay on South Australia's Fleurieu Peninsula tested positive for avian influenza (H5), according to the state's chief veterinary officer, who assessed the risk of an extensive outbreak among dolphins as low while flagging ongoing concern for seals and sea lions. South Australia has recorded 341 positive H5 events and Australia 732 confirmed events in wildlife as of 02 November 2026. New detections are less frequent, with no recent mass mortality. Vaccine has been released for wild little penguin colonies at Granite Island, Penneshaw and Emu Bay, with no start date set. H5 has not been reported from any Pacific Island country or territory to date. – Source: BEACON, HPAI detected in a dolphin, South Australia, Australia as federal government rolls out wildlife vaccination and Latest data - DAFF accessed on 03 November 2026. • Hawai’i: On 29 October 2026, the Hawaiʻi State Department of Health reported that genomic sequencing identified H5N1 genetic material, genotype D1.1, in a wastewater sample collected on 14 October 2026 at a site in East Kauaʻi. It is the first detection of this genotype in Hawaiʻi, where genotype A3 was previously found. The detection does not mean that live, infectious virus is or has been present in a human. No human case has been linked to this signal and no H5N1 has been detected in local dairy milk testing. – Source: Hawaiʻi Department of Health, DOH reports H5N1 avian flu detected in Kauaʻi County wastewater sample accessed on 03 November 2026. • Japan: A dead wild goose recovered in Kurihara City, Miyagi Prefecture, on 27 October 2026 tested preliminarily positive for avian influenza virus. The Environment Ministry is awaiting genetic confirmation of whether the strain is of high pathogenicity, which would be the first such detection in a wild bird in Japan this season. A 10 km priority zone for wild bird monitoring has been designated around the site. No poultry, mammal or human case has been reported. – Source: BEACON, First preliminary positive detection of avian influenza in a wild goose this migratory season in Japan accessed on 03 November 2026. Many thanks again for your continuous contributions. Please note that the alerts displayed on the map are based on information available to us as of the date of this report.

link_title: Project Wolbachia now covers more than half of all households in Singapore
link_description: SINGAPORE - A decade after being introduced, Project Wolbachia – an initiative to control dengue through the release of lab-grown mosquitoes – now covers over half of all households in Singapore. Following a launch in Ang Mo Kio on Oct 6, Project Wolbachia now covers more than 840,000 households – or 53% of all households here – covering most of the areas at risk of large dengue outbreaks. This was announced on Oct 31 by Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment Janil Puthucheary at an event marking the initiative’s 10th anniversary, held at Our Tampines Hub. Beginning in 2016, Project Wolbachia aims to control the Aedes mosquito population here via the release of male mosquitoes infected with the Wolbachia bacteria. Female mosquitoes that mate with these males produce eggs that do not hatch, thus reducing the mosquito population over time. In February, research published in the New England Journal of Medicine found that the Aedes aegypti mosquito populations were reduced by 80 to 90% in areas covered by Project Wolbachia, while the dengue risk for residents in these areas fell by over 70%. link_title: Circulating Zika and dengue IgA-NS1 marks early postnatal exposure without significant association with congenital Zika syndrome-related microcephaly
link_description: Elevated preexisting maternal IgG-NS1 to DENV, rather than to ZIKV, has been associated with a reduced risk of microcephaly in congenital Zika syndrome (CZS), suggesting a protective role. While serological analysis of IgG and IgM has physiological limitations in infants, IgA-NS1 represents a marker of host exposure to orthoflavivirus, as it is not transferred transplacentally and reflects early active immune responses. This study evaluated circulating IgA-NS1 responses to ZIKV and DENV in mothers and infants prenatally exposed to ZIKV in southern Colombia, a dengue hyperendemic region.MethodsIn this multicentric study, we analyzed 164 mother-infant pairs with confirmed gestational ZIKV exposure during the Colombia 2015-2016 epidemic. Using optimized ELISAs with well-characterized clinical samples, we simultaneously assessed circulating IgA-NS1 responses against ZIKV and DENV1-4. Neurological outcomes were evaluated through pediatric follow-up to determine associations between IgA-NS1 and CZS-related microcephaly.ResultsIgA-NS1 ELISAs for ZIKV and DENV1-4 achieved sensitivity/specificity of 94%/97% and 86%/85%, respectively. DENV-exposed samples showed 26% cross-reactivity against ZIKV NS1. There was no evidence of placental transfer, and IgA-NS1 levels for ZIKV and DENV were comparable between mothers and infants with or without CZS-related microcephaly. However, circulating ZIKV and DENV IgA-NS1 increased postnatally and were higher in older children.ConclusionWhile circulating IgA-NS1 serves as a promising postnatal marker of orthoflavivirus exposure in infants due to its stability and lack of placental transfer, it does not appear to contribute to protection against severe CZS outcomes. These findings demonstrate that protective NS1-mediated immunity against microcephaly may be isotype-dependent.

author: id-journal.bsky.social
text: Obesity ↑DENV binding Abs (FC 1.89) but no ↑ neutralizing Abs. Leptin↑ binding Abs (FC 1.22); adiponectin↓ (FC 0.79). Obesity = ↓neutralizing efficiency (FC 0.67).
link_title: Obesity in Children is Associated With Increased Dengue Virus Binding, but not Neutralizing, Antibody Responses Following Primary Infection
link_description: Obesity has been associated with higher risk of dengue virus (DENV) infection and disease, yet its influence on antibody responses to DENV remains undefined.MethodsWe evaluated whether nutritional status—based on body mass index z-score (BMIz)—or blood markers of body fat—leptin and adiponectin—are associated with binding and/or neutralizing antibody responses to DENV in 85 children in the Nicaraguan Pediatric Dengue Cohort Study who experienced a primary DENV infection in 2019. Associations were estimated using linear models adjusting for age, sex, and DENV infection outcome.ResultsCompared with children with normal weight, those with obesity had higher quantities of DENV binding antibodies (fold-change [FC] 1.89, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.02, 3.48) but no difference in neutralizing antibodies. Likewise, leptin concentration was associated with higher quantities of binding antibodies (FC 1.22, 95% CI 1.09, 1.37), while adiponectin was associated with lower quantities (FC 0.79, 95% CI .67, .94), and neither was associated with neutralizing antibodies. Lower neutralizing efficiency (neutralizing/binding antibodies) was observed in children with obesity (FC 0.67, 95% CI .48, .93).ConclusionsOur results indicate that obesity is associated with higher antibody quantity (binding) but not higher quality (neutralization) postprimary DENV infection—implying that antibodies generated by children with obesity have lower neutralization efficiency, requiring greater quantities to reach similar levels of neutralization than children with normal weight. Further, the agreement among the 3 models using distinct proxies of body fat—BMIz, leptin, and adiponectin—demonstrates that adipokines are useful in supplementing BMIz analysis or as independent predictors of immune responses.

Au cours de la semaine 42, 33 cas de fièvre éruptive aiguë ont été signalés au niveau national, contre 18 la semaine précédente : 16 dans le district de la Capitale nationale, 11 dans les Highlands orientales, 4 dans la province d’Enga, 1 en Nouvelle-Bretagne orientale et 1 dans la province de Simbu (426 cas et 396 échantillons testés à ce jour). La campagne de vaccination contre la rougeole et la rubéole continue de cibler tous les enfants de moins de sept ans vivant dans un district dans lequel un cas de rougeole ou de rubéole a été signalé dans le cadre d’activités de vaccination menées à l’occasion des contacts habituels avec les services de santé. L’alerte rouge pour la rougeole est maintenue en Papouasie-Nouvelle-Guinée. – Source : Département national de la santé de Papouasie-Nouvelle-Guinée, bulletin hebdomadaire sur les événements de santé publique, communiqué au point de contact du Groupe de coordination du ROSSP le 23 octobre 2026. Maladies respiratoires • Nouvelle-Calédonie : D’après le bulletin no 11 (daté du 23 octobre 2026) de la direction des Affaires Sanitaires et Sociales (DASS), l’épidémie de grippe se poursuit, mais décélère : on comptait 93 cas confirmés biologiquement au cours de la semaine épidémiologique 42 (du 12 au 18 octobre), contre 131 cas au cours de la semaine 41 et un pic à 151 cas au cours de la semaine 40. Le taux de positivité reste très élevé (57 %, contre 55 % au cours de la semaine 41) et la DASS appelle à la prudence, la baisse observée pouvant être partiellement liée aux vacances scolaires. Le sous-type A(H1N1)pdm09 reste largement prédominant (57 cas sur 93), et au 22 octobre, aucun nouveau cas de sous-type A(H3N2) n’avait été signalé. Le nombre de passages aux urgences est passé de 1 865 au cours de la semaine 41 à 1 505 au cours de la semaine 42 ; la proportion d’infections respiratoires aiguës a reculé de 13 % à 7 %. Les cas de grippe et de pneumonie étaient majoritaires (39 % et 26 %, respectivement). Le nombre de cas graves reste important, puisque 33 % des patients présentant un syndrome grippal ont été hospitalisés au cours de la semaine 42 (35 personnes), contre 28 % au cours de la semaine 41. En réanimation, le taux d’occupation des lits est inférieur au seuil de vigilance de 80 % depuis le 20 octobre, et se montait à 56 % le 22 octobre. L’alerte rouge pour la grippe A est maintenue. – Source : Direction des Affaires Sanitaires et Sociales de Nouvelle-Calédonie, Vigilance DASS bulletin 2026 no 11 sur l’épidémie de grippe, communiqué au point de contact du Groupe de coordination du ROSSP le 26 octobre 2026. • Nouvelle-Zélande : Au cours de la semaine qui s’est achevée le 18 octobre 2026, la grippe est restée le virus le plus couramment détecté chez les patients atteints d’une infection respiratoire aiguë sévère (IRAS) dans la région d’Auckland (11 échantillons positifs), suivie par le rhinovirus (9 cas). Le taux de positivité à la grippe est passé de 25,0 % à 20,4 % chez les patients atteints d’une IRAS. Chez les patients présentant un syndrome grippal pris en charge dans les cabinets de médecine générale du réseau de surveillance sentinelle, le taux de positivité est passé de 18,2 % à 6,7 %. En 2026, 24,0 % des échantillons IRAS (687 sur 2 860) étaient positifs à la grippe ; ce pourcentage s’établit à 18,9 % (225 sur 1 190) chez les généralistes du réseau sentinelle. Le sous-type A(H1) représentait 39,4 % cas d’IRAS positifs à la grippe, et le sous-type A(H3) 32,0 %. L’alerte bleue pour la grippe A est maintenue. – Source : PHF Science, tableau de bord des infections respiratoires aiguës sévères , page consultée le 27 octobre 2026. • Vanuatu : Le ministère de la Santé a déclaré une épidémie de grippe A sur l’île d’Efate (province de Shefa) à la suite d’une hausse du nombre de cas de syndrome grippal et de cas de grippe A confirmés biologiquement. D’après le ministère, 1 709 cas de syndrome grippal ont été recensés dans la province de Shefa, alors que le seuil d’alerte se situe à 223 cas. Le nombre hebdomadaire de cas est passé de 360 au cours de la semaine épidémiologique 39 à 535 au cours de la semaine 42. Les enfants de moins de 5 ans représentent 57 % des cas de syndrome grippal. Vingt-sept cas de grippe A ont été confirmés (2 au cours de la semaine 41, 25 au cours de la semaine 42), dix patients ont été hospitalisés (sept d’entre eux ont pu regagner leur domicile) et aucun décès n’a été signalé. L’hôpital national de Vanuatu a activé son centre d’intervention d’urgence, a établi un dispositif de triage spécifique pour les personnes présentant des symptômes grippaux et a restreint les visites. Au niveau national, le bulletin de surveillance syndromique pour la semaine 42 (du 12 au 18 octobre 2026) fait état de 1 185 cas de syndrome grippal, contre 964 au cours de la semaine 41, un chiffre supérieur au seuil d’alerte. Vingt-huit échantillons se sont révélés positifs à la grippe A. Une alerte rouge pour la grippe A est ajoutée pour Vanuatu. – Source : ministère de la Santé de Vanuatu, via Health Promotions Vanuatu , page consultée le 27 octobre 2026, et bulletin de surveillance des maladies syndromiques et à prévention vaccinale à Vanuatu, communiqué au point de contact du ROSSP le 26 octobre 2026. Rotavirus • États fédérés de Micronésie : Le bulletin hebdomadaire de l’État de Yap pour la semaine épidémiologique 42 (du 12 au 18 octobre 2026) mentionne une alerte aux maladies diarrhéiques pour la neuvième semaine consécutive, avec neuf cas (le seuil d’alerte se situant à sept). Des agents pathogènes entériques ont été identifiés chez quatre patients : co-infections par Salmonella , E. coli entéro-agrégatif et E. coli entéropathogène (EPEC et ETEC) mises en évidence par panel gastro‑intestinal BioFire chez trois malades, et adénovirus mis en évidence par test de diagnostic rapide chez un patient. Les recommandations de santé publique en matière de maladies diarrhéiques restent en vigueur. L’alerte bleue pour le rotavirus est maintenue pour les États fédérés de Micronésie (État de Yap). – Source : Département de la santé de Yap, rapport hebdomadaire sur les maladies transmissibles, communiqué au point de contact du Groupe de coordination du ROSSP le 23 octobre 2026. Autres informations : Dengue • Hawaii : Le 22 octobre 2026, le Département de la santé d’Hawaii a déclaré un nouveau cas de dengue lié à un voyage à Maui, sans lien avec les cas déjà signalés. Il s’agit du dixième cas rapporté à Hawaii en 2026. Le risque de transmission est considéré comme faible. – Source : Département de la santé d’Hawaii, DOH reports another travel-related dengue virus case , page consultée le 27 octobre 2026. « Une seule santé » – Virus Shamonda • France : Le 23 octobre 2026, le ministère de la Santé et Santé publique France ont fait état de la première détection du virus Shamonda chez l’être humain en France. Le patient, présentant une immunodépression sévère, a été pris en charge à Lyon pour une atteinte neurologique grave. Il est décédé. Le virus Shamonda est un Orthobunyavirus transmis aux animaux par des moucherons piqueurs du genre Culicoïdes, les bovins étant considérés comme les hôtes principaux parmi les espèces animales pouvant être infectées. Une nouvelle lignée s’est propagée en Europe depuis l’été 2026. Au 20 octobre 2026, le virus avait été détecté chez des bovins dans 52 départements français. Jusqu’alors, il était considéré comme non transmissible à l’humain. À ce stade, l’hypothèse privilégiée est celle d’une transmission par la piqûre d’un moucheron infecté. À ce jour, aucune transmission interhumaine ni aucun risque sanitaire pour la population générale n’a été identifié. Une enquête « Une seule santé » est en cours. – Source : Ministère de la Santé, Virus Shamonda : une première détection chez l’être humain et Santé publique France, Virus Shamonda : un premier cas humain détecté en France , pages consultées le 27 octobre 2026. link_description: TB preventive treatment benefits people with HIV in the ‘treat all’ era Providing tuberculosis (TB) preventive treatment (TPT) to people living with HIV is associated with fewer TB cases and deaths from all causes, according to a study in The Lancet HIV.1 The study examined its effectiveness in the “treat all” era, when antiretroviral therapy (ART) is recommended for everyone diagnosed with HIV. Researchers analysed electronic health records from more than 235,000 people with HIV in Haiti, Kenya, Nigeria, Uganda, Zimbabwe and Ukraine. The data were collected as part of the Programmatic Effectiveness of Tuberculosis Preventive Treatment for People with HIV in Six High-Tuberculosis-Burden Countries (PROTECT) prospective cohort study. According to the multinational research team, it is the largest real-world evaluation of TPT effectiveness among people with HIV. Across the six countries, starting TPT within eight weeks of entering HIV care was consistently associated with lower TB incidence and mortality. Overall, treatment was associated with a 61% reduction in TB incidence and a 45% reduction in deaths from all causes.
